summary: The note is an incident-style report on how aging utility infrastructure causes repeated power, water and internet disruptions in Cedar Heights, which it presents as an example of a national pattern. It collects quotes from residents, officials, economists and executives on economic, health, education and security impacts. It concludes that costly modernization, including smart grids and renewables, is urgent and needs federal involvement.
one_line: Report on how aging infrastructure causes repeated utility outages in Cedar Heights and why costly national modernization is urgently needed.
key_facts: Cedar Heights lost power on September 14, 2023, the third outage in as many months.
Edgar Thomson, spokesperson for Cedar Heights' municipal utilities, said on December 2, 2023 that the infrastructure dates back to the 1960s.
Octavia Smith, a Cedar Heights flower shop owner, has had to discard entire stocks of perishables because of storm-related outages.
Dr. Alexis Harper of the Hathaway Institute said on October 29, 2023 that short, frequent outages add up to significant economic disruption, a 'domino effect'.
Jennifer Castro said on November 10, 2023 that over half of utility lines and power plants are beyond their intended lifespan.
Retrofitting the nation's aging utility systems is described as a multitrillion-dollar venture.
The Cedar Heights City Council met on September 25, 2023 to discuss solutions, but funding remained unresolved.
Mayor Mariah Peterson called the problem 'a national challenge' and urged federal involvement.
Leonard Harris, CEO of QuickCom Telecommunications, said on January 8, 2024 that overhauling the network requires immense investment.
On November 25, 2023, Cedar Heights reported E. coli in its water supply due to pipe failures, causing a week-long boil order.
Teacher Lila Rodriguez said on December 15, 2023 that repeated outages caused canceled classes.
City technician Michael Johnson said on January 20, 2024 that infrastructure has become 'a patchwork quilt of repairs'.
General Emma Richardson warned in a February 1, 2024 security briefing that an unreliable grid is a national security risk.
David Nelson said on January 12, 2024 that the economy is approaching a tipping point without infrastructure investment.
